title: The change jar challenge: one jar, one goal, thirty days
description: Every coin and small note that reaches your pocket goes into the jar for a month. A tiny, visible savings habit with a goal written on the side.

body.heading: Set up the jar
paragraphs: Choose a clean jar with a lid and one specific goal small enough to reach: a family pizza night, a plant for the garden, a book you have wanted for months. Write the goal and the target amount on a label and stick it where everyone can see it.
Specific beats big. A jar for “savings” fills slowly and empties guiltily; a jar for “pizza night, $30” fills like it means it.

body.heading: The thirty-day rule
paragraphs: For thirty days, every coin that comes home in a pocket or purse goes into the jar that evening — no exceptions for the big coins, no borrowing back for parking. If your life is mostly card payments, use the digital version: round each purchase up to the nearest dollar in your banking app, or move a small fixed amount on coin days.
Empty pockets into the jar at the same moment each day — keys down, coins in — so the habit attaches itself to arriving home.

body.heading: Count day
paragraphs: On day thirty, tip the jar onto the table and count it together. Photograph the total, celebrate whatever it is, and spend it on the goal exactly as promised — the celebration is what makes the next jar fill faster.
Then choose the next goal while the jar is still empty and gleaming. Small money, visibly gathered, teaches more about saving than any lecture.

takeaway: One labelled jar, every coin for thirty days, and a goal small enough to celebrate: saving you can watch happening.
materials: A clean jar with a lid
A label and pen for the goal and target amount
A notebook or phone note for the day-thirty count
supervision: The household agrees the rule together — what goes in, and that nothing comes out until count day.
safetyNotes: Keep the jar somewhere visible but secure, and out of reach of small children, for whom coins are a choking hazard.
Count day spending follows the label: agree any change of goal together, out loud, before the jar is opened.
